title: SARS-CoV-2 Genome Sequencing Using Long Pooled Amplicons on Illumina Platforms
author: John-Sebastian Eden
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.befyjbpw
materials: elution tube (2 ml Eppendorf PCR clean, DNA LoBind)

Here we provide an example low throughput viral RNA extraction protocol; however, any platform that extracts viral or pathogen RNA (or total nucleic acid) should be suitable. We typically use the residual viral extracts from clinical samples following diagnostic RT-PCRs, which include extracts off both Qiagen BioRobot EZ1 and Roche MagnaPure 96 platforms. Please ensure appropriate PPE and containment to avoid exposure to infectious samples, noting that following the addition of the DNA/RNA Shield, the virus will be inactivated.
The amplicon primers are as follows:

Analyse 5 µL, each RT-PCR reaction on a 1% agarose gel with DNA staining dye. When using Invitrogen E-Gel 48 Agarose precast gels, preload each well with 10 μl of EB buffer. All bands are expected to be ~2.5kb, so run with an appropriate DNA ladder. To aid in pooling visualisation, it is preferable to run all set A and B reactions for one sample on the same row.
Following tagmentation, immediately remove the reaction from the thermocycler and add 2.5 µL, Neutralize Tagment Buffer (NT) to stop the reaction.

steps.title: Extract Viral RNA
steps.instruction: Extract viral RNA from samples using a Zymo-Spin IC column.

substeps.instruction: Add 400 µL Viral RNA Buffer to each 200 μl sample and mix by gentle vortexing.
Transfer mixture into a Zymo-Spin IC column in a collection tube; centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 2 minutes.
Transfer column to a new collection tube; add 500 µL Viral Wash Buffer and centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 30 seconds.
Transfer column to a new collection tube; repeat the wash step (add 500 µL Viral Wash Buffer, centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 30 seconds).
Add 500 µL Ethanol (95-100%) to the column and centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 2 minutes.
Transfer the column into a clean 2 ml Eppendorf PCR clean, DNA LoBind elution tube.
Add 25 µL DNase/RNase-Free Water directly to the column matrix, incubate for 5 minutes, and centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 30 seconds to elute RNA.
Store eluted RNA frozen at -80 °C or use immediately.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Prepare cDNA from viral RNA using SuperScript IV VILO Master Mix.

substeps.instruction: Set up the reaction mix for each sample and a no template control (NTC).
If using individual components instead of VILO mastermix, use a random hexamer primed reaction supplemented with oligo-dT to achieve a 3:1 random hexamer/oligo-dT ratio.
Incubate the reaction according to the specified (though not listed) parameters.
Keep cDNA on ice for immediate use or store frozen at -20 °C.

steps.title: Amplify Viral Genome Regions
steps.instruction: Perform parallel PCR to amplify 14 regions (~2.5kb each) across the viral genome.

substeps.instruction: Prepare primer sets by combining 4.5 µL forward primer (100 μM), 4.5 µL reverse primer (100 μM), and 171 µL nuclease free water.
Set up reaction mixes for each sample and NTC (14.5 reactions per sample to account for pipetting error).
Dispense 16.5 µL reaction mix into each well.
Add 1.5 µL viral cDNA into each well using an 8-channel multipipettor.
Add 2 µL of the diluted and premixed primer sets into each well.
Seal the plate and centrifuge for 30 seconds in a plate spinner.
Incubate the reaction according to the specified parameters.

steps.title: Pool and Purify Amplicons
steps.instruction: Pool the 14 amplicons per sample and purify using AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Pool individual amplicons into a single well, targeting a final volume of ~40 µL (approx 3 µL per amplicon).
Adjust final volume to 50 µL using clean EB buffer.
Add 40 µL room temperature AMPure XP beads (0.8X ratio) and pipette up and down 15 times.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Place on a magnetic stand for at least 2 minutes until clear; discard supernatant.
Perform two washes: add 200 µL freshly prepared 80% EtOH, incubate for 30 seconds, and discard supernatant.
Air dry beads for 5 to 15 minutes.
Remove from magnetic stand and resuspend pellet with 40 µL EB buffer; pipette up and down 15 times.
Place on magnetic stand for at least 2 minutes until clear and transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Store purified DNA frozen at -20 °C or use immediately.

steps.title: Quantify and Normalize DNA
steps.instruction: Quantify and adjust the concentration of purified DNA for library preparation.

substeps.instruction: Quantify DNA using Qubit dsDNA broad range assay.
For samples >10ng/μl, dilute with EB buffer to a concentration between 1 ng/μL and 10 ng/μL.
Re-quantify using Qubit dsDNA high sensitivity assay.
Dilute to 0.2 ng/μL using EB buffer (minimum total volume 20 µL).

steps.title: Prepare Illumina Nextera XT Library
steps.instruction: Prepare libraries using a modified Nextera XT protocol (halved volumes and manual normalization).

substeps.instruction: Combine 5 µL Tagment DNA Buffer (TD) and 2.5 µL pooled, diluted (0.2 ng/μl) amplicons; mix by pipetting 10 times.
Add 2.5 µL Amplicon Tagment Mix (ATM), mix by pipetting 10 times, seal and centrifuge.
Incubate according to specified parameters, then mix by pipetting 10 times, seal and centrifuge.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Add indices and Nextera PCR Master Mix (NPM) and incubate according to specified parameters.
Add 15 µL room temperature AMPure XP beads (0.6X ratio) to the 25 μl amplified libraries; pipette up and down 15 times.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Place on magnetic stand for at least 2 minutes until clear; discard supernatant.
Perform two washes: add 200 µL freshly prepared 80% EtOH, incubate for 30 seconds, and discard supernatant.
Air dry beads for 5 to 15 minutes.
Remove from magnetic stand and resuspend pellet with 22.5 µL EB buffer; pipette up and down 15 times.
Place on magnetic stand for at least 2 minutes until clear and transfer 20 µL supernatant to a new tube.
Quantify using Qubit dsDNA high sensitivity assay.

steps.title: Pool and Load Illumina Libraries
steps.instruction: Pool libraries by DNA amount and prepare for iSeq loading.

substeps.instruction: Pool individual libraries equally based on Qubit values.
Quantify the final pool using Qubit dsDNA high sensitivity assay.
Analyze 2 µL of the pool with Agilent High Sensitivity D5000 Screen Tape.
Calculate final molarity: (Tapestation DNA molarity) x (Qubit DNA conc / Tapestation DNA conc).
Dilute pooled libraries to 1 nM (at least 50μl) using EB buffer.
Dilute 20 µL of 1nM library pool with 80 µL EB buffer to reach 0.2 nM.
Load 20 µL of 0.2nM library pool into a defrosted Illumina iSeq cartridge and sequence (at least 75 nt paired end).

steps.title: Alternative Nanopore Sequencing Workflow
steps.instruction: Prepare and sequence libraries using the Oxford Nanopore Rapid Barcoding kit.

substeps.instruction: Perform Flow cell QC per Oxford Nanopore instructions.
For each sample, combine 100-200 fmol of pooled amplicons with 2.5 µL fragmentation mix.
Adjust final volume to 10 µL using Nuclease free water; mix and spin down.
Incubate at 30 °C for 1 minute, then at 80 °C for 1 minute; cool on ice.
Pool all samples into a 1.5 ml LoBind tube; mix and spin down.
Transfer 10 µL of pooled RBK004 libraries to a new 1.5 ml LoBind tube and add 1 µL RAP; mix and spin down.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes and store on ice.
Prime and load the Spot ON Flow Cell per Oxford Nanopore instructions.
Sequence for up to 2 hours or until sufficient data is obtained.

steps.title: Nanopore Bioinformatic Analysis
steps.instruction: Process Nanopore sequencing data to generate a consensus sequence.

substeps.instruction: Perform base calling, demultiplexing, and adaptor trimming using Guppy.
Filter reads using NanoFilt (min quality 10, max length 2,700 bases).
Map reads to reference genome MN908947.3 using Minimap2 and convert to sorted .bam using SAMtools.
Perform variant calling using medaka_variant; interrogate variants with QUAL score < 30.
Generate consensus sequence from the .vcf file using BCFtools.
